title: Platform Systems & Services: Team Wiki, Runbooks, Dashboards, Alerts, Roadmap & Q2 Retrospective
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview:

This page is the canonical team wiki for Platform Systems & Services. It centralizes the operational runbooks, dashboard and alert definitions, service inventory, ownership, short-term roadmap, and a brief Q2 2026 retrospective. Use this as the first stop for oncall, runbook creation, and onboarding new services to the platform.

Table of contents:
1. Purpose and scope
2. Ownership and SLOs
3. Systems & services inventory (summary)
4. How-tos & onboarding playbooks
5. Dashboards & alerting (key dashboards, alert thresholds)
6. Runbooks: incident triage and escalation
7. Q2 2026 retrospective highlights
8. Roadmap (next 3-6 months)
9. Team wiki conventions and templates
10. Change log / contributors

1) Purpose and scope
- Audience: platform engineers, SREs, service owners, and oncall responders.
- Scope: core platform infra (control plane, service mesh, kube clusters, GPU fleet, inference runtime), observability stack, and runbooks tied to customer-impacting SLOs.

2) Ownership and SLOs
- Platform control plane (service: redwood-control): owner: Platform Core (team lead: Diego Alvarez). SLA targets: Availability 99.95% monthly; latency P95 < 150ms for management API.
- Inference router (service: request-router): owner: Serving Runtime (team lead: Priya Rao). SLOs: P99 latency < 450ms for short-seq (<512 tokens) requests; error rate < 0.25% per rolling 30d.
- GPU fleet manager (service: gpu-manager): owner: Infra (team lead: Avery Chen). SLOs: Node availability 99.9% (per region); scheduling latency median < 3s.
- Telemetry & logs (service: observability-platform): owner: Eng Platform Observability (team lead: Maya Patel). SLOs: metrics ingestion success > 99.9%; alert delivery < 60s.

Ownership table (simple):
| Service | Short name | Owner team | Primary owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Control plane API | redwood-control | platform-core | Diego Alvarez |
| Request routing | request-router | serving-runtime | Priya Rao |
| GPU fleet manager | gpu-manager | infra | Avery Chen |
| Observability | observability-platform | eng-platform | Maya Patel |

3) Systems & services inventory (summary)
- Critical components: redwood-control, request-router, model-cache, kv-prefix-cache, quantization-service, gpu-manager, autoscaler, ingress-proxy, metrics-collector, alert-dispatcher.
- Dependency notes: request-router depends on model-cache and gpu-manager; autoscaler uses metrics-collector for utilization signals.

4) How-tos & onboarding playbooks
A. Onboard a new service to platform monitoring:
  1. Create service entry in service-registry (internal repo).
  2. Add Prometheus scrape job: /ops/monitoring/prometheus/scrape-jobs.yaml (example snippet below).
  3. Create Grafana dashboard skeleton using dashboard-template.json.
  4. Add alert rules to alerting repo (PR -> monitoring owner review).
  5. Add runbook (short playbook) in this wiki under /runbooks/<service-name>.

Prometheus scrape example (yaml snippet):
---
- job_name: 'request-router'
  static_configs:
    - targets: ['request-router.prod.cluster.internal:9100']
  relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_namespace]
      action: keep
      regex: 'redwood-*'
---

B. Deploying a control-plane patch (canary -> global):
  1. Create release branch and build image tag (CI pipeline: build-and-scan).
  2. Deploy to canary cluster (canary/namespace) with 2 replicas.
  3. Run smoke tests: management API health, auth, a short inference loop through request-router.
  4. Monitor key dashboards for 30m (latency, error-rate, CPU/mem).
  5. If green, increment canary to 10% traffic for 1 hour, then full rollout with rolling updates.
  6. If any critical alert fires, rollback to previous tag and open incident per runbook.

5) Dashboards & alerting
Key dashboards (names in Grafana):
- Platform Overview (dashboard id: platform-overview) - top-level KPIs (request rate, errors, P50/P95/P99 latency, cluster capacity, cost).
- GPU Fleet Health (gpu-fleet-health) - node up/down, GPU memory pressure, driver version mismatches, scheduler queue length.
- Runtime Performance (runtime-performance) - kv cache hit rate, model loading time, sequence-length distribution, token throughput.
- Observability Health (obs-health) - metrics ingestion rate, log retention, alert delivery latency.

Alerting: alert rules are stored in repo ops/monitoring/alerts. Primary notification channel is #oncall-platform with PagerDuty escalation for sev2/1.
Recommended thresholds (baseline, tuned Q2 2026):
- High error rate (sev2): service_error_rate(request-router) > 0.5% for 5m -> PagerDuty if sustained 10m.
- Latency degradation (sev2): p95_latency(request-router) > 600ms for 5m.
- Control plane down (sev1): redwood-control.health == 0 for 1m.
- GPU node loss (sev2): region_gpu_node_down_count > 2 for 10m.
- Metrics ingestion drop (sev2): metrics_ingest_rate < 70% of baseline for 5m.

Example Datadog/Prometheus alert rule (text):
ALERT RequestRouterHighErrorRate
  IF increase(request_router_errors_total[5m]) / increase(request_router_requests_total[5m]) > 0.005
  FOR 10m
  LABELS { severity="sev2" }
  ANNOTATIONS { summary="Request router error rate > 0.5%", runbook="/runbooks/request-router-high-error-rate" }

Notification policy:
- Sev1: page P0 oncall (Platform PagerDuty) and notify #eng-urgent.
- Sev2: page P1 oncall and notify #oncall-platform.
- Sev3: alert to Slack only, ticket for next-business-day triage.

6) Runbooks: incident triage and escalation
Runbook: request-router high error rate (short):
1. Initial check (first 5 minutes)
  - Confirm the alert in alert-dispatcher and Grafana.
  - Check recent deploys (CI/CD -> recent deployments to request-router).
  - Check request-router logs for error spikes (kubectl logs or log-search).
  - Check model-cache and gpu-manager dashboards for downstream failures.
2. Mitigation (if errors due to model load or resource exhaustion)
  - Scale up request-router by 2 replicas (kubectl scale).
  - If model-cache OOMs: restart model-cache pods one at a time.
  - If GPU shortage: trigger autoscaler policy to add reserved nodes, or divert traffic to fallback model variant via smart-router config.
3. Escalation
  - If mitigation fails in 15 minutes: escalate to oncall lead (phone/PagerDuty) and open incident in incident tracker.
  - Notify customer-success if impact scope shows >5% customer requests affected.
4. Post-incident
  - Run postmortem template within 72 hours; assign owners and action items.

7) Q2 2026 retrospective highlights (summary)
- Incidents: 3 Sev1 incidents in Q2 (one control-plane downtime due to certificate rotation bug; one broad telemetry ingest outage; one GPU fleet fragmentation after kernel rollforward).
- Root causes & actions completed:
  - Certificate rotation bug: root cause was missing staged cert for canary cluster. Action: implement automated cert preflight (completed 2026-05-22).
  - Telemetry ingestion outage: root cause was a cardinality explosion in metric labels from a new customer instrumenting models. Action: apply label sanitization rules in metrics-collector and enforce labels whitelist (done 2026-06-02).
  - GPU kernel rollforward issue: root cause was inconsistent driver versions in a subset of nodes. Action: add node-driver-version dashboard, gate kernel upgrades with staged rollout and automated driver verification (in progress, ETA 2026-07-10).
- Operational metrics improvements: mean time to acknowledge decreased from 9m -> 4.5m after oncall rotation change; alert noise reduced by ~18% after tuning alert rules.

8) Roadmap (next 3-6 months)
- July 2026: GPU driver verification pipeline and staged kernel rollout (owner: gpu-manager team).
- Aug 2026: Prefix/KV cache per-customer isolation feature and QA (owner: serving-runtime).
- Sep 2026: Observability hardening: label whitelist enforcement and per-tenant quota controls (owner: eng-platform-observability).
- Q4 planning: Dedicated autoscaling (predictive scaling) prototype for Dedicated customers; cost/reliability evaluation.

Priorities and criteria:
- Priority 1: anything affecting SLOs for hosted API or causing multi-customer impact.
- Priority 2: reliability and observability gaps that reduce incident time-to-detect.
- Priority 3: cost optimization features (batching, cache improvements) that do not regress quality.

9) Team wiki conventions and templates
- Doc title convention: <area>-<topic>-<year>-<quarter> (e.g., platform-runbook-request-router-2026-q2).
- Runbook template: short description, owner, detection signals, step-by-step mitigations, escalation path, post-incident actions.
- Dashboard template: summary panel, error/latency panels, resource utilization, related alerts, and a linked runbook.
- Labels taxonomy: platform, infra, runtime, observability, oncall, sla, roadmap. Use max 6 labels per page.

10) Change log / contributors

Appendix: links and quick commands
- Monitoring repos: git@repo.internal:ops/monitoring.git
- Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/platform-overview
- PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.redwood/incidents
- Quick kubectl checks:
  - kubectl -n request-router get pods
  - kubectl -n request-router logs -l app=request-router --tail=200
  - kubectl scale deployment request-router --replicas=<n>

If anything on this page is unclear or missing, please file a doc update PR or ping the eng-platform Slack channel.
